project.name: voice
project.description:
Self-hosted in-app voice/video calling (Phase 1 of the self-reliance initiative - browser-to-agent WebRTC via a self-hosted LiveKit server, zero PSTN, zero Twilio dependency; NOT related to core/omnichannel/twilio, which stays telephony-only and untouched).
New leaf-ish module rather than folding into "agents": token issuance is a genuinely separate concern (signs a LiveKit access token, no LLM/agent logic of its own) and this module deliberately depends ON agents/sarvam/ elevenlabs (to drive the STT -> AgentChatService -> TTS turn pipeline), not the reverse - putting it in "agents" would risk agents depending back on a brand-new provider integration for a capability most tenants won't use yet. Same one-directional-addition shape as eventbus/graphmemory/ devices (see core/pom.xml's module-order comment).
LiveKit access tokens are signed here directly via Nimbus JOSE+JWT (com.nimbusds:nimbus-jose-jwt) per LiveKit's documented HS256 JWT token spec, rather than pulling in LiveKit's own server SDK - nimbus-jose-jwt is already a transitive, compile-scope dependency of every module that depends on "security" (spring-boot-starter-oauth2-resource-server -> spring-security-oauth2-jose -> nimbus-jose-jwt), so this adds zero new third-party surface.
Depends on: security (TenantContext), tenancy (schema-per-tenant, no persistence of its own today but keeps this module's dependency shape consistent with every sibling provider-integration module), agents (AgentService for tenant-scoped agent lookup, AgentChatService for the text turn), sarvam (SarvamSpeechToTextClient - STT leg), elevenlabs (ElevenLabsClient/ElevenLabsVoiceService - TTS leg, reusing the existing voice-cloning integration exactly as the build brief specified).
storage (StorageProperties) was added for LiveKitEgressService - LiveKit's Egress API uploads directly to an S3-compatible endpoint via its own S3Upload config in the Egress request, so this module reuses the app's existing StorageProperties (bucket/credentials/endpoint) rather than inventing a second, parallel S3 config surface just for call recordings. spring-boot-starter-data-jpa/postgresql were added for VoiceCallRecording (a small tenant-schema table tracking each recording's egress id/object key) - both are already transitive via tenancy, declared explicitly here anyway for the same self-documenting-module reason omnichannel does the same for its own JPA entities.
